My personal favorite is sausage gravy. All in all it should take around 15 minutes.

1T Flour
1T Butter
1C milk
Chicken Bouillon to taste
1lbs Sausage (Seasoned to taste. Keep it savory though; no sweet stuff.)

First, cook the sausage. Get it all crumbly and into pretty small bits. 1/2 inch at the biggest.

In a separate pan, melt the butter and then throw in the flour. Get it all whisked up until it's in a kind of bubbly paste. Take the pan off the heat and add the milk. Remember, before you add the milk, DON'T let the roux get cold. I can't stress this enough. If the roux gets cold then when you add the milk it'll come out lumpy. Hot roux + cold milk = smooth gravy.

Keep whisking that shit up until it starts to boil, and then until it starts to thicken. Once it gets about as thick as you want it, turn off the heat and add in the sausage. Don't be afraid to let the sausage grease get in there too. Fat is flavor man. Anyway, mix in the sausage. and then add a shit load of pepper and some salt. Don't overdo the salt because if it sits in the fridge the flavors mix all together and after a while it'll get really salty. Then, add in the bouillon. Same with the salt, don't overdo this. Bouillon is salty so be careful.

Then you can just spoon that crap over whatever you want. My personal favorite is hash browns and eggs, but biscuits, toast, country steak, or whatever else you think might be good would work too.

Goes great with drop biscuits. No rolling or cutting required for these:

  • 2 cups flour
  • 1 Tbs baking powder
  • 1 Tbs sugar
  • 1/2 tsp salt
  • 1/2 cup melted butter
  • 1 cup milk

Mix dry ingredients. Add wet ingredients and stir just until it comes together. Don't overstir it or your biscuits will be tough. Drop dough in heaping tablespoons onto a greased baking sheet. Bake at 450 8-12 minutes, until edges are light brown. Cool slightly and smother with gravy.
